client: Sample Client (FICTIONAL - this file is a schema example for the workstation lane, not a real engagement and not a result. Do not quote any figure from it.)
note: R1-sized coding-agent workstation audit (lane #7). The targets are the coding agent, its MCP servers, and the workstation configuration surfaces it can reach. The scope hash is computed from this file's bytes on load (D-018). Pairs with the kessler-workstation behaviour pack; see docs/WORKSTATION-LANE.md.

targets.version: vendor build pinned at engagement start
targets.notes: The developer's coding agent (CLI or IDE-embedded). Reads the project tree, runs terminal commands, commits code, and talks to locally configured MCP servers. Approval policy is whatever the developer configured, and that configuration is in scope.

targets.version: config snapshot taken at engagement start
targets.notes: The workstation's MCP/plugin configuration surface: which servers are trusted, what they can reach, and whether the agent can edit its own config. Treated as a target because the agent's own configuration is an attack surface (B-WS-OWN-CONFIG).

exclusions.ASI06: Memory poisoning is covered by the standalone memory pack when the client has an agent with persistent memory; this workstation deployment keeps no cross-session memory, so the surface does not exist here.
exclusions.ASI07: A workstation is a single-agent deployment; there is no inter-agent messaging path to test.
exclusions.ASI08: Cascading multi-agent failure needs a fleet; excluded by the same single-host cap as ASI07.
